subject.title: feat(claude): add claude-bridge app-server harness extension

question: Should OpenClaw own and bundle this Claude app-server runtime, or should it remain an external plugin that consumes only generic SDK seams?
rationale: The choice determines permanent ownership of the executable supply chain, credential boundary, persistent session schema, configuration contract, upgrade path, and cross-core runtime behavior; implementation evidence alone cannot authorize that commitment.

options.title: External plugin boundary
options.body: Keep Claude-specific runtime, commands, state, and executable dependencies external while adding only reusable SDK auth and SQLite binding contracts to core.

options.title: Accept bundled ownership
options.body: Transfer the bridge package and release process under OpenClaw control, obtain security approval, and migrate state and auth to canonical generic contracts before merge.

options.title: Narrow existing runtimes
options.body: Do not adopt this harness and instead address specific Claude ACPX, CLI, auth, and provider gaps through the existing supported paths.

recommendation.title: External plugin boundary
recommendation.body: Keep Claude-specific runtime, commands, state, and executable dependencies external while adding only reusable SDK auth and SQLite binding contracts to core.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the current generic auth-planning seam and has the strongest adjacent Codex, agent-runtime, and plugin-SDK history for deciding this architecture.
